newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open mixed amid firm dlr, weak U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open mixed amid firm dlr, weak U.S..

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mixed in quiet trade on Friday amid weakness in U.S. fixed-income markets and further gains in the Canadian dollar overnight, analysts said.

"It looks like the U.S. market is going to cause a bit of grief for us since we got the (U.S.) housing numbers," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "Other than that, we're benefiting from the positive currency."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.05 percent from 3.04 percent at the close of trading on Thursday.

Canadian T-bills benefited as the dollar opened stronger at C$1.3660 (US$0.7320) in light trading as the currency continued to benefit from signs that the Bank of Canada was preparing to tighten monetary policy.
But weakness in U.S. markets after the release there of housing starts and building permits data for April weighed on the Canadian T-bill market, traders said.

Trading in the Canadian market was expected to remain light with many dealers leaving early in order to extend the holiday weekend. Canadian markets will be closed on Monday for the Victoria Day holiday.
"Wherever we are by eleven o'clock is where we're going to be until after auction Tuesday," the trader said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.38 percent from 3.36 percent on Thursday. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.85 percent from 3.87 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 2.95 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
